To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a brain protein inhibits the high affinity binding sites for GABA; 2) the endogenous inhibitor is a 15,000 dalton protein; 3) the endogenous inhibitory protein is a selective antagonist of the high affinity GABA receptor, and 4) diazepam and the endogenous inhibitor act on the same site of the GABA receptor.
a thermostable, endogenous protein of about 15000 MW is an endogenous inhibitor of high affinity GABA receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of action of the benzodiazepinic drugs.
the molecular basis of the interaction of diazepam with GABA receptors.
the molecular mechanisms of the action of benzodiazepinergic ligands on the GABA receptors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the endogenous protein inhibitor is an endogenous ligand which is a natural antagonist for benzodiazepinergic receptors and that diazepam is an exogenous agonist for the same receptor, which is coupled to the high affinity GABA receptor.
the endogenous protein is the endogenous ligand for the GABA receptor.

the endogenous protein inhibitor and the benzodiazepinergic ligand (benzodiazepines and their enantiomers) are acting at the same receptor site and the endogenous protein may be the natural benzodiazepinic ligand.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
diazepam and other benzodiazepinones act on the GABA receptor by binding to a specific site which is distinct from the site that binds GABA.
the endogenous protein inhibitor is a natural ligand for benzodiazepinic receptors.
the brain has a natural ligand for benzodiazepinic receptors and that the action of diazapam is mediated by its ability to counteract the action of this ligand.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is no evidence that GABAergic transmission is involved in the anxiolytic action of benzodiazepenes, and that the endogenous protein inhibitor may be a natural ligand for brain benzodiazepene receptors.
we have identified an endogenous inhibitor that regulates GABA receptor activity.
the GABA receptor is composed of at least 2 types of receptors, one of which has a high affinity for GABA and is blocked by an endogenous inhibitor.
